messages:
emily: Hi finance team — quick one from my trip to Berlin. I withdrew cash from an ATM on my personal card to pay for a shared taxi and small event expenses. Bank applied a 3.5% foreign transaction fee + a 2.5 EUR ATM surcharge. Total withdrawn: €200, my statement shows amount charged $216.80 due to DCC. Receipt uploaded to Ramp: https://ramp.app/receipts/berlin-atm-001 (screenshot attached). Filing as 'Cash - personal card (travel)'.

rob: thanks emily. couple clarifying q's: 1) did the ATM offer Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC) asking to charge in USD vs EUR? 2) did you get an ATM receipt with the EUR amounts listed? we need to know the original euro amount for FX conversion validation.

emily: yep the ATM had a prompt and I accidentally selected USD because it showed a cleaner number. ATM receipt attached shows "Dispensed €200" and an on-screen DCC confirmation line saying "Amount in USD: $216.80". I should have picked EUR but missed it.

sara: per policy we do reimburse out-of-pocket travel expenses but we don't cover avoidable DCC fees. card-ops, any levers to reverse or dispute DCC charges with the issuing bank?

card-ops: DCC is a merchant-side option. Banks can sometimes reverse an extra markup if we dispute promptly and show the original EUR receipt and documentation proving the better rate was available. However, reversals are not guaranteed and can take 30-60 days. If employee selected DCC, issuer may say it's user choice.

rob: okay. two paths: 1) employee-requested exception: manager can approve reimbursing the DCC markup if there was confusion and travel context justifies it; 2) finance can reimburse only the EUR-equivalent using mid-market FX on the date of the ATM withdrawal and deny the DCC markup. emily do you want us to calculate reimbursement based on the official EUR amount and decline the DCC markup?

emily: I'd prefer we reimburse the EUR-equivalent and note the DCC as employee mistake. I can try disputing with my bank as well but want to avoid double-tracking.

sara: @rob please calculate EUR->USD amount using OANDA rate for 2026-05-11 and process reimbursement for that amount. We'll mark the DCC fee as denied as avoidable. Also add a quick note to emily's Ramp entry explaining policy to avoid DCC in future.

card-ops: I'll add a short internal note in the corpcard guide about DCC pitfalls. Also FYI we can share a one-liner in the travel checklist to "Always select local currency (EUR, GBP, etc.) when prompted".

finance-bot: Action items: 1) Rob to compute reimbursement = amount based on EUR200 at FX rate on 2026-05-11; 2) Deny DCC markup from reimbursement; 3) Emily to attach ATM dispense receipt and any screenshots to Ramp (already attached). After processing, expect reimbursement in 3-5 business days.

rob: computed amount and updated Ramp comment: reimbursing $205.12 (EUR200 @ 1.0256 mid-market on 2026-05-11). Denying DCC markup $11.68. Manager Sara approved denial rationale. Processing now.

emily: thanks all — makes sense. i'll be more careful next time :grimacing:

sara: thanks for the quick follow-up. we'll also circulate the DCC note in the travel prep doc.
